description: Eight looping sample players on a field, with five clocks and eight effects: a player sounds only while a clock is near it, and picks up every effect near it

params.text: Moves that player left and right on the field, which is also its position in the stereo picture
Moves that player up and down on the field
Sets how likely that player is to load a different sample, rolled on every quarter note; the mapping is exponential, so the low settings are genuinely rare and it starts at about one roll in ten
Halves, leaves or doubles that player's playback rate, on top of the global speed knob
Mutes that player, keeping its clock and its couplings so it returns in time; the same control is its lamp, coloured by the division it is bound to and violet while muted
Loads a different sample into that player at once, without waiting for a change roll
Glides every clock between the two rolled positions it owns, so one knob moves the whole timing weather across the field
Glides every effect between the two rolled positions it owns
Sets the radius round every clock and every effect at once: small is a sparse drizzle, large a downpour, since it sets how many players hear a clock and how many effects each picks up
Sets how strongly players that line up pull on each other: vertically towards a common playback phase, horizontally towards a common loop window at half that rate, diagonally into an occasional swap
Sets the master tempo, 1 to 250 beats per minute, on an exponential travel so the bottom is a beat a minute and the top puts a thirty-second note every 30ms
Multiplies every player's playback rate, 0.1x to 2x; on the sparse engine it also thins the rain, because a grain played twice as fast is over in half the time
Sets the longest a loop window may be, 0.1 to 3 seconds; on the sparse engine it is also how long one drop lasts
Sets how likely a skip is on each eighth note, 0% to 100%
Sets the playback rate of the skip voice, 0.5x to 2x
Sets the level of the skip voice
Sets the decay of the reverb every player near it is treated by, 0.3 seconds to 10 seconds
Sets the output level, -38dB to +8dB, into a soft limiter that will not pass -1dBFS
Sets how likely the micro voice is to sound on each beat of its division
Collapses three of the original's controls into one: at the bottom of its travel one micro sound repeats on a fixed grid, at the top the sound, its variation and the division itself are all shifting
Sets the level of the micro voice
Chooses the division the micro voice rolls on: 2n, 4n, 8n, 16n or 32n
Reduces the bit depth of everything, with dither and a high-pass after it
Mixes in band-limited noise, gated open by the signal itself so it is not a constant hiss
Adds tape wow, flutter and age to everything
Mutes and freezes the whole engine, fading rather than cutting
Rolls new pairs of positions for the five clocks, on a jittered grid so a roll can never leave the field dead
Takes one small drunk step on every clock position in both constellations, so the field shifts and nothing is lost
Rolls new pairs of positions for the eight effects
Takes one small drunk step on every effect position in both constellations
Rerolls both constellations, randomises every knob except the volume, and reseeds the timing walks; the mute switches are left alone
Renders a whole new bank of sounds in the background; the old bank keeps playing until the new one is ready, with a progress bar in the display
Spreads the eight players back out into a tidy grid

inputs.text: Moves the players left and right: one channel per player on a polyphonic cable, and a mono cable moves all eight at once; five volts covers half the field
Moves the players up and down, one channel per player or all eight from a mono cable
Added to the clock morph knob; ten volts covers its whole travel
Added to the effect morph knob; ten volts covers its whole travel
Added to the reach knob; ten volts covers its whole travel
Added to the couple knob; ten volts covers its whole travel
A rising edge rolls new clock positions
A rising edge nudges the clock positions
A rising edge rolls new effect positions
A rising edge nudges the effect positions
Moves the tempo, one volt per octave, so one volt doubles it; it can push past the knob's top up to 500 beats per minute
Added to the speed knob; five volts covers its whole travel
Added to the micro probability knob; ten volts covers its whole travel
Added to the bitcrush knob; ten volts covers its whole travel
Added to the noise knob; ten volts covers its whole travel
Added to the tape knob; ten volts covers its whole travel
Added to the reverb length knob; ten volts covers its whole travel
A rising edge does what the randomize button does
A rising edge renders a new bank of sounds

outputs.text: A two-millisecond pulse on each edge of that division, jittered by the same bounded random walk the voices hear, so outside gear locks to this module's time rather than to a metronome
The skip voice on its own, before the master chain
The micro voice on its own, before the master chain
The left side of everything, after the master chain

notes: nothing here is loaded from disk. The whole bank is synthesized at seed time by a background thread, from about twenty-two loop archetypes and fourteen micro ones.
a player sounds only when a clock is inside the reach radius, the nearest one winning, and that clock's division sets how fast its loop window churns.
the effects stack in a fixed order for every player that is near them: reverse, low-pass, high-pass, band-pass, bitcrush, delay, granular, reverb.
retuning with Root or Scale rebuilds all 192 buffers from the same seed, so the field keeps its world and only its pitch moves, and the sounding players crossfade onto the new bank.
the position of a dot on the field is the whole arrangement: it fixes which clock the player is bound to, which effects treat it, and where it lands in the stereo picture.
menu: Engine — original, the default, where the players loop continuously and a clock edge only churns the loop window, or sparse, where an edge plays one pass through the window and then silence
Ephemeral — off by default, so the seed and both constellations are saved and a reload sounds the same; on, nothing is saved and every load rolls a new bank
Root — the note the whole generated bank is tuned to
Scale — one of fifteen scales the whole bank is snapped to, D minor pentatonic by default; the chord beds follow it too
